# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1142._

> ℹ️ **19 resolved thread(s) excluded; 25 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Suggested fix:** record the author login in the marker fields (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the commenter identity) and have `_markerObject`/`parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured `machineAuthor` allowlist (the action already resolves `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` — pass it into the probe). Fail closed the same way `classifyArmActor` now does.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a transplant interrupted after `open_pr` never reconciles — the source stays open forever with only a noop every tick**

The step order is `merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr`. If anything fails **between** `open_pr` and `close_pr` (a failed comment post, a failed close, a network blip), the state on the next tick is: source open with `po_accept`, armed marker, and an **open machine PR on the branch**.

That state is caught here, in `_transplantRefuseDecision`:

```js
if (input.openTransplantPr ||
    (input.marker && input.marker.state === 'transplanted')) {
    return { decision: 'noop', reason: 'already-transplanted', steps: [], ... };
}
```

- `openTransplantPr` truthy → permanent `noop`. The remaining steps (carry probe, transplant comment, source close) are **never re-run** — the AC1 close+comment lands only if a human closes the source by hand.
- The machine PR proceeds through validate/merge lanes **without the carried verdicts** (the carry labels, if due, were never applied), and the guest source PR stays open alongside it.
- Every subsequent tick re-queries the source and re-logs the same noop — silent, audit-only.

The decision core otherwise handles both neighbors of this gap well (pre-`open_pr` orphans complete via E5; post-close markers noop correctly). This is the only uncovered partial-failure window. Consider a reconciliation branch: when `openTransplantPr` exists **and** the marker is still `armed` (not `transplanted`), resume from `carry_decision` with the existing PR number instead of noop-ing.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the AC5 arm-actor classifier fails open when the machineAuthor allowlist is unconfigured**

```js
var logins = machineAuthorModule.machineAuthorLogins(
    Array.isArray(machineLogins) ? machineLogins.join(',') : machineLogins);
if (!logins.length) return 'human';   // ← ANY actor with a login reads as human
```

`machineAuthor` unconfigured → empty allowlist → every labeled-event actor (including any bot with write access) classifies as `'human'` and **arms the transplant**. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1142
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1142
- **Title**: gh-1140 [GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1140` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +3108
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T14:26:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T18:03:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Suggested fix:** record the author login in the marker fields (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the commenter identity) and have `_markerObject`/`parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured `machineAuthor` allowlist (the action already resolves `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` — pass it into the probe). Fail closed the same way `classifyArmActor` now does.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a transplant interrupted after `open_pr` never reconciles — the source stays open forever with only a noop every tick**

The step order is `merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr`. If anything fails **between** `open_pr` and `close_pr` (a failed comment post, a failed close, a network blip), the state on the next tick is: source open with `po_accept`, armed marker, and an **open machine PR on the branch**.

That state is caught here, in `_transplantRefuseDecision`:

```js
if (input.openTransplantPr ||
    (input.marker && input.marker.state === 'transplanted')) {
    return { decision: 'noop', reason: 'already-transplanted', steps: [], ... };
}
```

- `openTransplantPr` truthy → permanent `noop`. The remaining steps (carry probe, transplant comment, source close) are **never re-run** — the AC1 close+comment lands only if a human closes the source by hand.
- The machine PR proceeds through validate/merge lanes **without the carried verdicts** (the carry labels, if due, were never applied), and the guest source PR stays open alongside it.
- Every subsequent tick re-queries the source and re-logs the same noop — silent, audit-only.

The decision core otherwise handles both neighbors of this gap well (pre-`open_pr` orphans complete via E5; post-close markers noop correctly). This is the only uncovered partial-failure window. Consider a reconciliation branch: when `openTransplantPr` exists **and** the marker is still `armed` (not `transplanted`), resume from `carry_decision` with the existing PR number instead of noop-ing.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

```js

    Array.isArray(machineLogins) ? machineLogins.join(',') : machineLogins);
if (!logins.length) return 'human';   // ← ANY actor with a login reads as human
```

`machineAuthor` unconfigured → empty allowlist → every labeled-event actor (including any bot with write access) classifies as `'human'` and **arms the transplant**. Combined with `query.notMachine` — which is documented as inert when no machineAuthor is configured (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:1114`) — a deployment that sets `smGuestTransplant` but not `machineAuthor` has **no machine-actor check at all** on the one gate whose docblock calls the label "the voucher for executing foreign code in our CI".

I understand this is deliberate (test-pinned at `test_guestTransplant.js:705`) and consistent with the machineAuthor degradation doctrine for *review/rework* gates. But those gates degrade to "no auto action" on empty allowlists, while this one degrades to "**auto-execute foreign code**" — the opposite direction. Please confirm the intent; if confirmed, this can stay as-is (downgrading to a docs nit). If not, an empty allowlist should return `'unverified'` here — the one gate that arms untrusted code should be the fail-closed one, matching the module's own header ("missing proof refuses — fail closed").

- **PR #**: 1142
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1142
- **Title**: gh-1140 [GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1140` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +3108
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T14:26:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T18:03:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[po_accept by a human] --> R[rule guest-transplant: transplantSequence]
  R -->|machine/proof-less actor| X[refuse - audit only]
  R -->|conflict 409 / no-ref| P[park blocked + parked-head marker - #633 re-arm]
  R -->|eligible| B[refs API: ai/guest-N at main]
  B --> M[merges API: recorded source SHA]
  M --> PR[machine PR guest #N + Co-authored-by + carry iff identical diff]
  PR --> G[Security Gate jobs first - needs: wiring asserted]
  G --> V[validate-fresh then merge-validated - standard lanes]
  V --> GC[PR closed/merged - branch GC deletes ai/guest-N]
```

</details>

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Suggested fix:** record the author login in the marker fields (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the commenter identity) and have `_markerObject`/`parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured `machineAuthor` allowlist (the action already resolves `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` — pass it into the probe). **dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a transplant interrupted after `open_pr` never reconciles — the source stays open forever with only a noop every tick**

The step order is `merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr`. If anything fails **between** `open_pr` and `close_pr` (a failed comment post, a failed close, a network blip), the state on the next tick is: source open with `po_accept`, armed marker, and an **open machine PR on the branch**.

That state is caught here, in `_transplantRefuseDecision`:

```js

}
```

The decision core otherwise handles both neighbors of this gap well (pre-`open_pr` orphans complete via E5; post-close markers noop correctly). This is the only uncovered partial-failure window. ```js

    Array.isArray(machineLogins) ? machineLogins.join(',') : machineLogins);
if (!logins.length) return 'human';   // ← ANY actor with a login reads as human

`machineAuthor` unconfigured → empty allowlist → every labeled-event actor (including any bot with write access) classifies as `'human'` and **arms the transplant**. But those gates degrade to "no auto action" on empty allowlists, while this one degrades to "**auto-execute foreign code**" — the opposite direction. Please confirm the intent; if confirmed, this can stay as-is (downgrading to a docs nit). If not, an empty allowlist should return `'unverified'` here — the one gate that arms untrusted code should be the fail-closed one, matching the module's own header ("missing proof refuses — fail closed").

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1142
- **Title**: gh-1140 [GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1140` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +3108
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T14:26:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T18:03:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[po_accept by a human] --> R[rule guest-transplant: transplantSequence]
  R -->|machine/proof-less actor| X[refuse - audit only]
  R -->|conflict 409 / no-ref| P[park blocked + parked-head marker - #633 re-arm]
  R -->|eligible| B[refs API: ai/guest-N at main]
  B --> M[merges API: recorded source SHA]
  M --> PR[machine PR guest #N + Co-authored-by + carry iff identical diff]
  PR --> G[Security Gate jobs first - needs: wiring asserted]
  G --> V[validate-fresh then merge-validated - standard lanes]
  V --> GC[PR closed/merged - branch GC deletes ai/guest-N]
```

</details>

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Suggested fix:** record the author login in the marker fields (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the commenter identity) and have `_markerObject`/`parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured `machineAuthor` allowlist (the action already resolves `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` — pass it into the probe). Fail closed the same way `classifyArmActor` now does.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a transplant interrupted after `open_pr` never reconciles — the source stays open forever with only a noop every tick**

The step order is `merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr`. If anything fails **between** `open_pr` and `close_pr` (a failed comment post, a failed close, a network blip), the state on the next tick is: source open with `po_accept`, armed marker, and an **open machine PR on the branch**.

That state is caught here, in `_transplantRefuseDecision`:

```js
if (input.openTransplantPr ||
    (input.marker && input.marker.state === 'transplanted')) {
    return { decision: 'noop', reason: 'already-transplanted', steps: [], ... };
}
```

- `openTransplantPr` truthy → permanent `noop`. The remaining steps (carry probe, transplant comment, source close) are **never re-run** — the AC1 close+comment lands only if a human closes the source by hand.
- The machine PR proceeds through validate/merge lanes **without the carried verdicts** (the carry labels, if due, were never applied), and the guest source PR stays open alongside it.
- Every subsequent tick re-queries the source and re-logs the same noop — silent, audit-only.

The decision core otherwise handles both neighbors of this gap well (pre-`open_pr` orphans complete via E5; post-close markers noop correctly). This is the only uncovered partial-failure window. Consider a reconciliation branch: when `openTransplantPr` exists **and** the marker is still `armed` (not `transplanted`), resume from `carry_decision` with the existing PR number instead of noop-ing.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the AC5 arm-actor classifier fails open when the machineAuthor allowlist is unconfigured**

```js
var logins = machineAuthorModule.machineAuthorLogins(
    Array.isArray(machineLogins) ? machineLogins.join(',') : machineLogins);
if (!logins.length) return 'human';   // ← ANY actor with a login reads as human
```

`machineAuthor` unconfigured → empty allowlist → every labeled-event actor (including any bot with write access) classifies as `'human'` and **arms the transplant**. Combined with `query.notMachine` — which is documented as inert when no machineAuthor is configured (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:1114`) — a deployment that sets `smGuestTransplant` but not `machineAuthor` has **no machine-actor check at all** on the one gate whose docblock calls the label "the voucher for executing foreign code in our CI".

I understand this is deliberate (test-pinned at `test_guestTransplant.js:705`) and consistent with the machineAuthor degradation doctrine for *review/rework* gates. But those gates degrade to "no auto action" on empty allowlists, while this one degrades to "**auto-execute foreign code**" — the opposite direction. Please confirm the intent; if confirmed, this can stay as-is (downgrading to a docs nit). If not, an empty allowlist should return `'unverified'` here — the one gate that arms untrusted code should be the fail-closed one, matching the module's own header ("missing proof refuses — fail closed").

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

💡 **SUGGESTION: conflict detection by substring can misclassify any transport error as a merge conflict**

- The 27-CC `transplantSequence` was red even at 100 % statement coverage (CRAP = CC when fully covered), so the fix is behavior-preserving decomposition, not test-only work. Two helpers introduced by the first decomposition pass (`_labeledEventFor` CC 9, the shortened `transplantSequence` CC 10) were still over threshold and were split/trimmed further — every function now measures ≤ 8 at 100 % coverage.

- Coverage-gap tests added first (TDD): the carried-labels branch of `guestPrBody`, the stateless-marker skip in `parseTransplantMarker`, the seen-set cycle guard in `transitivelyNeeds`, the empty-allowlist path of `classifyArmActor`, the >60-char/empty-login fallbacks of `sanitizeCoAuthor`, and a direct `matchesGuards` guard table (`prState` / `prMergeState` / merge-state lists / `crossRepo` true-path in-chain) — the suite grew 52 → 59 transplant tests (+166 smGithubSource file total).

## Approach

Every fix keeps the public module surface (`module.exports`) and all decision strings byte-identical; only internal composition changed.

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `matchesGuards` stays a flat guard table: the three merge-state guards collapsed behind one composite `_mergeStateGuardsFail`, `mergeable` + `prState` behind `_prStateGuardsFail` (CC 19 → 16, CRAP 19.1 → 16.0).

  - `gcSteps` (10 → 3) → `_gcEntryStep` / `_orphanStep`.
  - `guestPrTitle` (9 → 7): the duplicated `(cfg && cfg.titleMaxLen) || DEFAULTS.titleMaxLen` cap expression hoisted to one `cap` local (same value in both uses).

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions

- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

- **PR #**: 1142
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1142
- **Title**: gh-1140 [GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1140` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +3108
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T14:26:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T18:03:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[po_accept by a human] --> R[rule guest-transplant: transplantSequence]
  R -->|machine/proof-less actor| X[refuse - audit only]
  R -->|conflict 409 / no-ref| P[park blocked + parked-head marker - #633 re-arm]
  R -->|eligible| B[refs API: ai/guest-N at main]
  B --> M[merges API: recorded source SHA]
  M --> PR[machine PR guest #N + Co-authored-by + carry iff identical diff]
  PR --> G[Security Gate jobs first - needs: wiring asserted]
  G --> V[validate-fresh then merge-validated - standard lanes]
  V --> GC[PR closed/merged - branch GC deletes ai/guest-N]
```

</details>

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Suggested fix:** record the author login in the marker fields (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the commenter identity) and have `_markerObject`/`parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured `machineAuthor` allowlist (the action already resolves `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` — pass it into the probe). Fail closed the same way `classifyArmActor` now does.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a transplant interrupted after `open_pr` never reconciles — the source stays open forever with only a noop every tick**

The step order is `merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr`. If anything fails **between** `open_pr` and `close_pr` (a failed comment post, a failed close, a network blip), the state on the next tick is: source open with `po_accept`, armed marker, and an **open machine PR on the branch**.

That state is caught here, in `_transplantRefuseDecision`:

```js
if (input.openTransplantPr ||
    (input.marker && input.marker.state === 'transplanted')) {
    return { decision: 'noop', reason: 'already-transplanted', steps: [], ... };
}
```

- `openTransplantPr` truthy → permanent `noop`. The remaining steps (carry probe, transplant comment, source close) are **never re-run** — the AC1 close+comment lands only if a human closes the source by hand.
- The machine PR proceeds through validate/merge lanes **without the carried verdicts** (the carry labels, if due, were never applied), and the guest source PR stays open alongside it.
- Every subsequent tick re-queries the source and re-logs the same noop — silent, audit-only.

The decision core otherwise handles both neighbors of this gap well (pre-`open_pr` orphans complete via E5; post-close markers noop correctly). This is the only uncovered partial-failure window. Consider a reconciliation branch: when `openTransplantPr` exists **and** the marker is still `armed` (not `transplanted`), resume from `carry_decision` with the existing PR number instead of noop-ing.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the AC5 arm-actor classifier fails open when the machineAuthor allowlist is unconfigured**

```js
var logins = machineAuthorModule.machineAuthorLogins(
    Array.isArray(machineLogins) ? machineLogins.join(',') : machineLogins);
if (!logins.length) return 'human';   // ← ANY actor with a login reads as human
```

`machineAuthor` unconfigured → empty allowlist → every labeled-event actor (including any bot with write access) classifies as `'human'` and **arms the transplant**. Combined with `query.notMachine` — which is documented as inert when no machineAuthor is configured (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:1114`) — a deployment that sets `smGuestTransplant` but not `machineAuthor` has **no machine-actor check at all** on the one gate whose docblock calls the label "the voucher for executing foreign code in our CI".

I understand this is deliberate (test-pinned at `test_guestTransplant.js:705`) and consistent with the machineAuthor degradation doctrine for *review/rework* gates. But those gates degrade to "no auto action" on empty allowlists, while this one degrades to "**auto-execute foreign code**" — the opposite direction. Please confirm the intent; if confirmed, this can stay as-is (downgrading to a docs nit). If not, an empty allowlist should return `'unverified'` here — the one gate that arms untrusted code should be the fail-closed one, matching the module's own header ("missing proof refuses — fail closed").

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

💡 **SUGGESTION: conflict detection by substring can misclassify any transport error as a merge conflict**

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1142
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1142
- **Title**: gh-1140 [GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1140` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +3108
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T14:26:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T18:03:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[po_accept by a human] --> R[rule guest-transplant: transplantSequence]
  R -->|machine/proof-less actor| X[refuse - audit only]
  R -->|conflict 409 / no-ref| P[park blocked + parked-head marker - #633 re-arm]
  R -->|eligible| B[refs API: ai/guest-N at main]
  B --> M[merges API: recorded source SHA]
  M --> PR[machine PR guest #N + Co-authored-by + carry iff identical diff]
  PR --> G[Security Gate jobs first - needs: wiring asserted]
  G --> V[validate-fresh then merge-validated - standard lanes]
  V --> GC[PR closed/merged - branch GC deletes ai/guest-N]
```

</details>

_Previous review discussions for PR #1142._

> ℹ️ **19 resolved thread(s) excluded; 25 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)


## General PR Comments

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Suggested fix:** record the author login in the marker fields (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the commenter identity) and have `_markerObject`/`parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured `machineAuthor` allowlist (the action already resolves `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` — pass it into the probe). Fail closed the same way `classifyArmActor` now does.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a transplant interrupted after `open_pr` never reconciles — the source stays open forever with only a noop every tick**

The step order is `merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr`. If anything fails **between** `open_pr` and `close_pr` (a failed comment post, a failed close, a network blip), the state on the next tick is: source open with `po_accept`, armed marker, and an **open machine PR on the branch**.

That state is caught here, in `_transplantRefuseDecision`:

```js
if (input.openTransplantPr ||
    (input.marker && input.marker.state === 'transplanted')) {
    return { decision: 'noop', reason: 'already-transplanted', steps: [], ... };
}
```

- `openTransplantPr` truthy → permanent `noop`. The remaining steps (carry probe, transplant comment, source close) are **never re-run** — the AC1 close+comment lands only if a human closes the source by hand.
- The machine PR proceeds through validate/merge lanes **without the carried verdicts** (the carry labels, if due, were never applied), and the guest source PR stays open alongside it.
- Every subsequent tick re-queries the source and re-logs the same noop — silent, audit-only.

The decision core otherwise handles both neighbors of this gap well (pre-`open_pr` orphans complete via E5; post-close markers noop correctly). This is the only uncovered partial-failure window. Consider a reconciliation branch: when `openTransplantPr` exists **and** the marker is still `armed` (not `transplanted`), resume from `carry_decision` with the existing PR number instead of noop-ing.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the AC5 arm-actor classifier fails open when the machineAuthor allowlist is unconfigured**

```js
var logins = machineAuthorModule.machineAuthorLogins(
    Array.isArray(machineLogins) ? machineLogins.join(',') : machineLogins);
if (!logins.length) return 'human';   // ← ANY actor with a login reads as human
```

`machineAuthor` unconfigured → empty allowlist → every labeled-event actor (including any bot with write access) classifies as `'human'` and **arms the transplant**. Combined with `query.notMachine` — which is documented as inert when no machineAuthor is configured (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:1114`) — a deployment that sets `smGuestTransplant` but not `machineAuthor` has **no machine-actor check at all** on the one gate whose docblock calls the label "the voucher for executing foreign code in our CI".

I understand this is deliberate (test-pinned at `test_guestTransplant.js:705`) and consistent with the machineAuthor degradation doctrine for *review/rework* gates. But those gates degrade to "no auto action" on empty allowlists, while this one degrades to "**auto-execute foreign code**" — the opposite direction. Please confirm the intent; if confirmed, this can stay as-is (downgrading to a docs nit). If not, an empty allowlist should return `'unverified'` here — the one gate that arms untrusted code should be the fail-closed one, matching the module's own header ("missing proof refuses — fail closed").

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

💡 **SUGGESTION: conflict detection by substring can misclassify any transport error as a merge conflict**

```js
if (msg.indexOf('Merge conflict') !== -1 || msg.indexOf('conflict') !== -1 ||
    msg.indexOf('409') !== -1) {
```

Any error thrown anywhere in the step list whose message merely *contains* `409` or `conflict` (a rate-limit page quoting a status, a proxy error, gh output echoing text that happens to include those substrings) swaps in the AC4 park plan — labeling the source `blocked` and closing nothing — instead of surfacing the real failure. Only the `merge` step can legitimately 409. Consider catching the conflict **at the merge step** (where `eMerge` is already in scope) and rethrowing a typed marker (e.g. `eMerge.isMergeConflict = true` set after checking the HTTP status), so the park decision can't be triggered by unrelated steps.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the GC slice takes the first N branches before knowing whether they are actionable**

```js
var names = out.split('\n')...
    .slice(0, cfg.maxGcBranches || 10);
```

The window is lexicographic and applied **before** the actionability probe, so:

- `ai/guest-10` sorts before `ai/guest-2`, and
- an OPEN-transplant-heavy prefix (each entry costs a find-PR probe and yields `null` in `_gcEntryStep`) starves the GC of branches further down the list — with >10 live guest branches, closed-PR branches can sit undeleted indefinitely.

Consider scanning the full (paginated) name list, evaluating entries until `maxGcBranches` **actionable** steps are collected — the same over-scan-until-actionable shape the conflict-rework rule adopted for its gh-1027 starvation fix.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `list[0]` arbitrarily picks which PR's state decides the GC**

```js
if (Array.isArray(list) && list.length) prState = String(list[0].state || '').toUpperCase();
```

**Fixed — same finding as thread 13, now landed on this head** (see the full fix description there; this is the re-assertion of the unauthenticated markers at `_markerObject`).

`parseTransplantMarker` now takes the machineAuthor allowlist and trusts only comments whose **author login** is in it (the `readVerdictRecords` spelling — `user.login || author.login || author.name`, lowercased, `[bot]` stripped); no/empty allowlist or an author-less comment parses to no marker, so a guest-forged newest `armed` marker is inert — the feed reads as "no marker" and the fresh path re-arms from the human label event. The wiring passes `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` on every probe (action, sweep orphan probe, `completionRentry` re-entry). Writers stamp `actor` for audit — but the trust anchor is the comment author, precisely because the payload (including any field in it) is guest-writable. The sweep's `complete_orphan` handler (`sweepClosedGuestBranches`, `js/smAgent.js`) now, before re-entering the action:

1. probes the source's current label names (`gh pr view <n> … --json labels`, new pure builder `buildPrLabelsCommand` + wiring probe `guestPrLabels`);

# pr-1142 rework — CI `crap` quality gate fixed (9 owned CRAP violations)

## Issues/Notes

- The failed check on head `7b246940` is the **`crap` job** (`.github/workflows/quality.yml`): the per-function CRAP ratchet (crap4js, threshold 8) compares the head against the rolling `crap-baseline` release asset — "CRAP may only decrease".
- The log fetch failed on the CI side (`host callback returned invalid JSON`), so the job was **reproduced locally with the exact pinned toolchain** (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee620`, `nyc@17`, the released `crap-baseline.json` @ `main@f3782b2b`, same instrument → suite → ratchet procedure). The local ratchet block matched CI's verdict line-for-line (exit code 2, `CRAP may only decrease.`):
  - `REGRESSION js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::matchesGuards: 18.1 -> 19.1`
  - `REGRESSION js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 28 -> 30`
  - `NEW > 8` in `js/common/guestTransplant.js`: `guestPrTitle: 9`, `guestPrBody: 8.5`, `parseTransplantMarker: 12`, `parseLabelEvents: 14`, `validateGateWiring: 10`, `transplantSequence: 27`, `gcSteps: 10`
- The 27-CC `transplantSequence` was red even at 100 % statement coverage (CRAP = CC when fully covered), so the fix is behavior-preserving decomposition, not test-only work. Two helpers introduced by the first decomposition pass (`_labeledEventFor` CC 9, the shortened `transplantSequence` CC 10) were still over threshold and were split/trimmed further — every function now measures ≤ 8 at 100 % coverage.
- No open review threads exist (GraphQL census `graphqlTotal: 0`; the only listed thread is the informational bot red-head marker, excluded by policy), so no `review_replies` entries are due.
- Coverage-gap tests added first (TDD): the carried-labels branch of `guestPrBody`, the stateless-marker skip in `parseTransplantMarker`, the seen-set cycle guard in `transitivelyNeeds`, the empty-allowlist path of `classifyArmActor`, the >60-char/empty-login fallbacks of `sanitizeCoAuthor`, and a direct `matchesGuards` guard table (`prState` / `prMergeState` / merge-state lists / `crossRepo` true-path in-chain) — the suite grew 52 → 59 transplant tests (+166 smGithubSource file total).

## Approach

Every fix keeps the public module surface (`module.exports`) and all decision strings byte-identical; only internal composition changed.

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `matchesGuards` stays a flat guard table: the three merge-state guards collapsed behind one composite `_mergeStateGuardsFail`, `mergeable` + `prState` behind `_prStateGuardsFail` (CC 19 → 16, CRAP 19.1 → 16.0).
  - `queryPrs` (CC 30 → 26, CRAP 30.0 → 26.0): the gh-1140 `allowBlockedItems` branches moved into module-level `_blockedHoldVisible` / `_blockedQueryHoldFail`, and the inline `mutexMax` expression now reuses the pre-existing `_mutexMaxOf(q)` helper.
- `js/common/guestTransplant.js` — the decision core decomposed so each AC/edge case lives in one ≤ 8-CC helper:
  - `transplantSequence` (CC 27 → 8) → `_transplantSkipDecision` / `_transplantRefuseDecision` / `_parkResetDecision` / `_orphanDecision` / `_freshSequence`; the orchestrator resolves `cfg`/`source`/`base` once and walks the helpers in the original decision order.
  - `parseTransplantMarker` (12 → 8) → `_markerObject` (one comment body → marker-or-null)…

- **PR #**: 1142
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1142
- **Title**: gh-1140 [GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1140` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +3108
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T14:26:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T18:03:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[po_accept by a human] --> R[rule guest-transplant: transplantSequence]
  R -->|machine/proof-less actor| X[refuse - audit only]
  R -->|conflict 409 / no-ref| P[park blocked + parked-head marker - #633 re-arm]
  R -->|eligible| B[refs API: ai/guest-N at main]
  B --> M[merges API: recorded source SHA]
  M --> PR[machine PR guest #N + Co-authored-by + carry iff identical diff]
  PR --> G[Security Gate jobs first - needs: wiring asserted]
  G --> V[validate-fresh then merge-validated - standard lanes]
  V --> GC[PR closed/merged - branch GC deletes ai/guest-N]
```

</details>

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Suggested fix:** record the author login in the marker fields (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the commenter identity) and have `_markerObject`/`parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured `machineAuthor` allowlist (the action already resolves `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` — pass it into the probe). Fail closed the same way `classifyArmActor` now does.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a transplant interrupted after `open_pr` never reconciles — the source stays open forever with only a noop every tick**

The step order is `merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr`. If anything fails **between** `open_pr` and `close_pr` (a failed comment post, a failed close, a network blip), the state on the next tick is: source open with `po_accept`, armed marker, and an **open machine PR on the branch**.

That state is caught here, in `_transplantRefuseDecision`:

```js
if (input.openTransplantPr ||
    (input.marker && input.marker.state === 'transplanted')) {
    return { decision: 'noop', reason: 'already-transplanted', steps: [], ... };
}
```

- `openTransplantPr` truthy → permanent `noop`. The remaining steps (carry probe, transplant comment, source close) are **never re-run** — the AC1 close+comment lands only if a human closes the source by hand.
- The machine PR proceeds through validate/merge lanes **without the carried verdicts** (the carry labels, if due, were never applied), and the guest source PR stays open alongside it.
- Every subsequent tick re-queries the source and re-logs the same noop — silent, audit-only.

The decision core otherwise handles both neighbors of this gap well (pre-`open_pr` orphans complete via E5; post-close markers noop correctly). This is the only uncovered partial-failure window. Consider a reconciliation branch: when `openTransplantPr` exists **and** the marker is still `armed` (not `transplanted`), resume from `carry_decision` with the existing PR number instead of noop-ing.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the AC5 arm-actor classifier fails open when the machineAuthor allowlist is unconfigured**

```js
var logins = machineAuthorModule.machineAuthorLogins(
    Array.isArray(machineLogins) ? machineLogins.join(',') : machineLogins);
if (!logins.length) return 'human';   // ← ANY actor with a login reads as human
```

`machineAuthor` unconfigured → empty allowlist → every labeled-event actor (including any bot with write access) classifies as `'human'` and **arms the transplant**. Combined with `query.notMachine` — which is documented as inert when no machineAuthor is configured (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:1114`) — a deployment that sets `smGuestTransplant` but not `machineAuthor` has **no machine-actor check at all** on the one gate whose docblock calls the label "the voucher for executing foreign code in our CI".

I understand this is deliberate (test-pinned at `test_guestTransplant.js:705`) and consistent with the machineAuthor degradation doctrine for *review/rework* gates. But those gates degrade to "no auto action" on empty allowlists, while this one degrades to "**auto-execute foreign code**" — the opposite direction. Please confirm the intent; if confirmed, this can stay as-is (downgrading to a docs nit). If not, an empty allowlist should return `'unverified'` here — the one gate that arms untrusted code should be the fail-closed one, matching the module's own header ("missing proof refuses — fail closed").

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

💡 **SUGGESTION: conflict detection by substring can misclassify any transport error as a merge conflict**

{"content":"# pr-1142 rework — CI `crap` quality gate fixed (9 owned CRAP violations)

Two helpers introduced by the first decomposition pass (`_labeledEventFor` CC 9, the shortened `transplantSequence` CC 10) were still over threshold and were split/trimmed further — every function now measures ≤ 8 at 100 % coverage.

## Approach

Every fix keeps the public module surface (`module.exports`) and all decision strings byte-identical; only internal composition changed.

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `matchesGuards` stays a flat guard table: the three merge-state guards collapsed behind one composite `_mergeStateGuardsFail`, `mergeable` + `prState` behind `_prStateGuardsFail` (CC 19 → 16, CRAP 19.1 → 16.0).

  - `transplantSequence` (CC 27 → 8) → `_transplantSkipDecision` / `_transplantRefuseDecision` / `_parkResetDecision` / `_orphanDecision` / `_freshSequence`; the orchestrator resolves `cfg`/`source`/`base` once and walks the helpers in the original decision order.
  - `parseTransplantMarker` (12 → 8) → `_markerObject` (one comment body → marker-or-null).
  - `parseLabelEvents` (14 → 4) → `_parsedEventList` / `_labeledEventFor` / `_eventActorLogin`.
  - `validateGateWiring` (10 → 4) → `_jobsByIdOf` / `_wiringViolations`.
  - `gcSteps` (10 → 3) → `_gcEntryStep` / `_orphanStep`.
  - `guestPrTitle` (9 → 7): the duplicated `(cfg && cfg.titleMaxLen) || DEFAULTS.titleMaxLen` cap expression hoisted to one `cap` local (same value in both uses).
  - `guestPrBody` (8.5 → 8.0): behavior unchanged; the uncovered carried-verdicts branch is now covered by a test (CRAP = CC = 8 at 100 % coverage).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1142
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1142
- **Title**: gh-1140 [GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1140` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +3108
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T14:26:13Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T18:03:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[po_accept by a human] --> R[rule guest-transplant: transplantSequence]
  R -->|machine/proof-less actor| X[refuse - audit only]
  R -->|conflict 409 / no-ref| P[park blocked + parked-head marker - #633 re-arm]
  R -->|eligible| B[refs API: ai/guest-N at main]
  B --> M[merges API: recorded source SHA]
  M --> PR[machine PR guest #N + Co-authored-by + carry iff identical diff]
  PR --> G[Security Gate jobs first - needs: wiring asserted]
  G --> V[validate-fresh then merge-validated - standard lanes]
  V --> GC[PR closed/merged - branch GC deletes ai/guest-N]
```

</details>

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`parseTransplantMarker`/`_markerObject` (this line and `guestTransplant.js:246`) accept **any** comment whose body carries the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check. But the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR** — they can comment on it freely, and the marker format is public (it's spelled out in this repo's source).

**Attack window.** Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after a tick that died between the arm-marker comment and the merge), the guest posts:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

with a `SHA_RE`-valid sha of any addressable commit — including code pushed to their fork *after* the human reviewed it. Next tick the core reads the forged marker as the newest snapshot and `_freshSequence` transplants **that** sha: E1's "the RECORDED sha at arm time, no TOCTOU" guarantee is only as strong as the marker's authorship, and here authorship is unverified. (Command injection is *not* possible — every consumption site re-validates through `resolveTransplantSha`'s `SHA_RE` or the `create_ref` 40-hex check; the impact is bounded to transplanting arbitrary guest-chosen content into the machine-PR channel.)

Bounded, but real: the human's label vouched for a specific reviewed diff; the machine transplants an attacker-chosen one. The verdict-carry check (AC6) fails closed on the drifted diff and the Security Gate ordering is the runtime boundary — but the gate checker itself is not wired into the shipped flow (separate thread), so the practical boundary for the redirected diff is just the project's ordinary pipeline.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated verbatim in `js/smAgent.js:6301-6304`: *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Suggested fix:** record the author login in the marker fields (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the commenter identity) and have `_markerObject`/`parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured `machineAuthor` allowlist (the action already resolves `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` — pass it into the probe). Fail closed the same way `classifyArmActor` now does.
